issues.legal_issue: An instrument executed in one state is not duly stamped there merely because it bears stamps issued in accordance with the law of another state.
material_facts: The mortgage deed was executed in one state, related to property in another state, and was later received in the latter state for registration.
The deed bore stamps issued under the law of the state where the property was situated, but not the stamps required by the law and rules of the state where it was executed.
Officers of the state of execution considered whether the deed was duly stamped under that state's law.
issues.conclusion: The deed was not duly stamped under the law of the state where it was executed, and the officers were right to treat it as not duly stamped; the petitioners were not entitled to relief.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(ii) of the Indian Stamp Act, an instrument is duly stamped only when it bears stamps of the proper amount and description used in accordance with the applicable law. Section 3, as amended in the state of execution, made execution there a dutiable event. Rule 3, made effective as part of the Act through sections 74–76, required the state's designated stamps. Stamps valid under another state's law did not satisfy that requirement. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.instrument_executed_in_assessing_state: The instrument was executed within the state whose officers assessed whether it was duly stamped.
predicates.assessing_state_requires_local_stamps: The law and rules applied by those officers required stamps issued or designated for use in that state.
predicates.foreign_state_stamps_only: The instrument bore stamps issued under another state's law and did not bear the stamps required by the assessing state.

issues.definition: When an instrument is executed in a state whose law requires its own designated stamps, stamps from another state alone do not make it duly stamped under the executing state's law.

issues.legal_issue: When an instrument becomes liable to duty on execution in one state and later becomes liable on receipt in another state, the second state may require only the additional duty where its rate is higher, and no further duty where its rate is the same or lower.
material_facts: The deed was executed in one state and thereby became liable to duty there.
The deed related to property in another state and was received there for registration, creating a further basis for duty under that state's law.
The Court considered the treatment of duty already paid in the first state when the second state's rate is higher, the same, or lower.
issues.conclusion: The instrument must first be stamped in accordance with the law of the state where it was executed. If the second state's rate is higher, only the excess duty is payable there, using stamps required by that state; if its rate is the same or lower, no further duty is payable there.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3, as amended in the relevant states, provided for liability arising on execution in one state and for further liability when an instrument relating to property or matters in another state was received there. Section 19A addressed the additional duty payable when the second state's rate was higher, and Rule 3 prescribed the stamps for that additional duty. The Court construed the scheme to mean that no further duty is payable where the second state's rate is the same or lower. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: instrument_chargeable_on_execution_in_first_state and later_received_in_second_state and first_state_duty_paid_under_local_law and (second_state_rate_higher or second_state_rate_same_or_lower)

predicates.instrument_chargeable_on_execution_in_fi: The instrument became liable to stamp duty because it was executed in the first state.
predicates.later_received_in_second_state: The instrument was later received in a second state and became liable to duty there under that state's law.
predicates.first_state_duty_paid_under_local_law: The duty arising in the first state was paid using stamps in accordance with that state's law and rules.
predicates.second_state_rate_higher: The duty rate applicable in the second state exceeded the rate applicable in the first state.
predicates.second_state_rate_same_or_lower: The duty rate applicable in the second state was the same as or lower than the rate applicable in the first state.

issues.definition: For an instrument first chargeable on execution and later received in another state, payment under the first state's law means that the second state can collect only the excess if its rate is higher, and nothing further if its rate is the same or lower.
